input: Root summary of enumeration attempt 003 (capture not yet copied): device info passed (count 5, 05ac:0341, reason 0, all spans valid). The interface-info response was CRC-valid, flags 40, device d0, command 20, report 02, subdevice 01, response_length matching, but id 0 where the request id was 1, so it stopped at response-identity M1KBD_STATUS -6. The global once-latch held: one sole claim plus 'probe refused' on re-match.
analysis: Requests use a global counter (PDM1SPIHID nextID++): device info id 0, interface info id 1. The device answered both with id 0, so 'the response echoes the request id' is refuted; the earlier device-info match was coincidental.

The reference (core.c:149-150) documents the id as 'a separate counter for each message type'. Outbound requests use a global msg_id++ (core.c:309), and process_response never compares ids. The observations fit a device-side per-type counter starting at 0 after the spien reset, but one sample cannot distinguish it from other id schemes, so no expected-id rule is supported.
Attempt 003 also confirms that the count limit was the sole attempt-002 cause: every string span was valid, so the old string check would have passed.
verdict_on_root_proposal: APPROVE. Removing id equality is not a blind relaxation under the stated invariants: (1) exactly one outstanding request, written and then waited for within the 1 s bound; (2) the three enumeration keys (0x20,0x01,0xd0), (0x20,0x02,0x01) and (0x20,0x10,0x01) are distinct and each is issued at most once per boot, with no retry; (3) the first flags-0x40 message after the write must match flags 40, device d0, command 20 and the exact report and subdevice, otherwise stop. 0x20 input messages remain counted and ignored. Under these invariants a stale or duplicate response always carries a different key and stops the attempt, so the id would add no disambiguation. This is preferable to an expected per-type id, which would rest on an unproven counter model.
conditions: Enforce invariant (2) in code, for example a small set of used (report, subdevice) keys checked before dlsp_request that refuses a repeat, rather than relying on call order alone.
Keep response_length diagnostic only. It matched in both samples, but the reference ignores it, so making it strict is unsupported.
Log the request id and response id as separate numeric fields, and rename the 'expected response' line to 'pending request' (key plus request id) so it no longer implies an echo.

Expect the next stage, the descriptor request (0x20,0x10,0x01, rsplen 512), to be the first hardware exercise of multi-packet reassembly if the descriptor exceeds one fragment. The engine is bounded and already reviewed.
not_claimed: No descriptor, IOHID publication, input or typing.
